def: The fixed 64-byte NVMe command record (sixteen Command Dwords, CDW0–CDW15) that the host writes into a Submission Queue and the controller fetches.
The 16-byte record the controller writes into a Completion Queue when a command finishes: command-specific result, SQ head pointer, SQ identifier, command identifier, phase tag and status.
A ring of SQEs in host memory (or a controller memory buffer) into which the host places commands and whose tail it announces through a doorbell register.
A ring of CQEs in host memory into which the controller writes completions; the host consumes entries using the phase tag and reports progress through the CQ head doorbell.
A 16-bit value chosen by the host in CDW0 bits 31:16 and returned in the CQE; unique among commands outstanding on the same Submission Queue, so (SQID, CID) identifies a command.
CDW1 of an NVMe command: the namespace the command acts on. 0 is not a valid namespace; FFFFFFFFh is the broadcast value where a command allows it.
Bytes 24–39 of an SQE: either PRP Entry 1 and PRP Entry 2, or one 16-byte SGL descriptor, selected by the PSDT field, describing the host data buffer.

exp: PRP or SGL for Data Transfer
def: CDW0 bits 15:14 of an SQE: 00b selects PRPs; 01b and 10b select SGLs with two interpretations of the Metadata Pointer; 11b is reserved.

Extra bytes stored with each logical block (for example protection information), transferred either interleaved with the data (extended LBA) or in a separate buffer addressed by the Metadata Pointer (MPTR).
CQE Dword 2 bits 15:0: the controller's current head of the Submission Queue named in the CQE, telling the host which SQ slots have been consumed and may be reused.
CQE Dword 3 bit 16. The controller inverts the value it writes on each pass through the Completion Queue, so the host can tell new entries from stale ones without clearing memory.
Three bits of the CQE Status Field: 0h generic, 1h command specific, 2h media and data integrity errors, 3h path related, 7h vendor specific. Qualifies the Status Code (SC).
The top bit of the CQE Status Field. When set, resubmitting the same command is expected to fail again.
Identify command CDW10 bits 7:0: selects which 4 KiB data structure to return (00h namespace, 01h controller, 02h active namespace ID list, 03h namespace identification descriptors, and others).
The admin command that returns a 4096-byte description of the controller, a namespace or a list, selected by CNS; the basis of capability discovery.

Reads a log page selected by its Log Page Identifier, with a 0's based Dword count (NUMDU:NUMDL) and an optional offset; used for error, SMART/health, firmware, changed-namespace, effects, self-test and telemetry logs.

An admin command the controller keeps outstanding until an enabled event occurs; its completion Dword 0 gives the event type, information and the log page to read. Not to be confused with PCIe Advanced Error Reporting.
Identify Controller byte 77: the largest data transfer of one command, as a power of two in units of the minimum memory page size (CAP.MPSMIN); 0 means no limit is reported.
The index of a fixed-size logical block in a namespace, from 0 to NSZE − 1. The block size is 2^LBADS bytes of the LBA format in use.
The 64-bit first logical block address of an NVM I/O command, in CDW10 (low) and CDW11 (high).
CDW12 bits 15:0 of NVM I/O commands: the number of blocks, 0's based (0 means one block).
CDW12 bit 30 of Read and Write: the command's data must be written to (or read from) non-volatile media before completion, not merely a volatile cache.
CDW12 bits 29:26 of NVM I/O commands: PRACT (controller inserts/strips protection information) and PRCHK (which of guard, application tag and reference tag the controller checks).

A per-block tuple in the metadata — in the classic format a 16-bit CRC guard, 16-bit application tag and 32-bit reference tag — that lets host and controller detect corrupted or misplaced data. Types 1–3 differ in how the reference tag is used.
An NVM I/O command carrying up to 256 LBA ranges with attributes; with Attribute – Deallocate set it is the NVMe equivalent of TRIM/UNMAP.
Identifies the I/O command set a namespace uses in the NVMe 2.x architecture; 0h is the NVM Command Set.
A device reading or writing host memory itself, without the CPU copying data; NVMe controllers use DMA (PCIe Memory Read/Write requests) for commands, data and completions.
The largest data payload a PCIe TLP may carry on a link, configured in the Device Control register (e.g. 256 bytes). Not to be confused with NVMe CC.MPS (memory page size).
A 64-bit pointer to a host memory page used by NVMe to describe data buffers: PRP1 (may include an offset), PRP2 (second page or pointer to a PRP list), and PRP lists for larger transfers.
